clue.text: Make a move to accept king's confession

indicators.note: to accept means one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: to make a move is to shift
R stands for king (Latin rex)

explanation.surface: A chess player edges a piece forward so the king can be taken, then owns up.
explanation.walkthrough: SHRIFT is an old word for confession to a priest, as in 'short shrift'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrift is the archaic term for confession and absolution given by a priest.

clue.text: Researcher's short break opens old wound

indicators.note: opens means this piece splits the other one open

parts.note: a scar is the mark of an old wound
hol is a short form of holiday, a break

explanation.surface: An academic's brief holiday reopens an old injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned person engaged in study and research.

clue.text: Happen again on bishop accepting gold coin

indicators.note: accepting means taking something inside

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is a bishop's title
the ecu was an old French gold coin

explanation.surface: A coin is presented to a bishop a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is only a link here, not RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To recur is to occur again, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Day to gain entrance to ship

parts.note: Fri is short for Friday
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: Someone chooses a day to get aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A frigate is a type of warship.

clue.text: Oddly afraid of hotplate in illustration

indicators.note: in means the cooker part goes inside the picture word

parts.note: PIC is short for picture, an illustration
a hob is the hotplate on top of a cooker

explanation.surface: Someone is strangely scared of the cooker shown in a drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like an alternate-letter signal on hotplate, but it belongs to the definition: an irrational fear.
explanation.definitionFit: A phobia is an irrational, abnormal fear, so being phobic is being unreasonably afraid.

clue.text: Instrument concealing priest's deformity

indicators.note: concealing means holding the other word out of sight inside

parts.note: the harp is a musical instrument
Eli is the priest in the biblical book of Samuel

explanation.surface: A musical instrument hides a cleric's physical defect.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleft lip, once commonly so called, is a congenital deformity.

clue.text: Close companion fled with bowel trouble

indicators.note: trouble means the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A friend ran off suffering from a stomach upset.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedfellow is someone closely associated with another, an intimate companion or ally.

clue.text: Hood muffling measure of noise heard in the Alps

indicators.note: muffling means wrapping around something to deaden it

parts.note: a cowl is a monk's hood
the bel is a unit of sound intensity

explanation.surface: A hood deadens a loud sound echoing in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine cattle wear clanking bells, a characteristic mountain sound.

clue.text: God's big flag

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, very big
the flag is the yellow iris, a plant

explanation.surface: A deity owns a huge banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' is not a banner but the iris plant; 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris is the Egyptian god of the dead and the afterlife.

clue.text: It's a crisis, if fast food has come from upstairs

definitions.meaning: an idiom for the moment when things are serious and decisive

definitions.text: fast food has come from upstairs
definitions.meaning: a whimsical literal reading: fried potatoes have been brought down

explanation.surface: Someone observes that a crisis has come because fried food has been sent downstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a critical moment of crisis; read literally it means fried potatoes have descended.

clue.text: Girl's part in mass

definitions.meaning: a girl's name, with the 's as 'is'
a section of the liturgy of the Mass, the hymn of praise

explanation.surface: A young woman has a role in a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female first name and also the name of the Glory to God hymn sung in the Mass.

clue.text: Glad to have repeated experience without point

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word goes round the compass letter

parts.note: to relive is to experience again
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone is happy to have done something again without any real purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but here means 'outside', putting RELIVED around E.
explanation.definitionFit: Relieved means glad and freed from worry, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Source of bureaucratic rules absurdly restricting Heads of State?

definitions.text: Source of bureaucratic rules absurdly restricting Heads of State?

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter
restricting means hemming in, so one group of letters surrounds the other
absurdly means the letters of rules are shaken into a nonsense order

parts.note: S is short for state; plural heads gives two of it

explanation.surface: A eurosceptic grumble that EU red tape ties the hands of national leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: Brussels, seat of the European Commission, is blamed for rules that bind national leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: The Belgian capital is home to the European Commission, the proverbial source of red tape for member states.

clue.text: Personal sign of soldier's upstanding character

indicators.note: upstanding in a down clue means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier; GI's gives GIS
one's nature is one's character

explanation.surface: A trooper's upright personality is a mark of who he is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upstanding' looks like praise but reverses GIS to SIG.
explanation.definitionFit: A signature is a person's own name written as their individual mark.

clue.text: Turn plate into fortune with a little medicine

indicators.note: into means these letters are put inside the money word

parts.note: a pile is a fortune, a lot of money
a U-turn, so U stands for turn
an L-plate is the learner's plate on a car

explanation.surface: Someone tries to turn a dinner plate into riches with a small dose of a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver displays an L-plate, so plate gives L.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilule is a small pill, literally a little dose of medicine.

clue.text: Neptune overdoes intake of silver

indicators.note: intake of means the metal is taken in by the turned word
over signals turning the following word over, back to front

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: The sea deity takes in too much silver.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'overdoes' must be split in two, 'over' as the reversal signal and 'does' as its fodder; 'intake of' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune is the Roman deity ruling the oceans.

clue.text: Record permitted to include gold decoration

indicators.note: to include means taking another piece inside

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
let means permitted
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: An official register is allowed to list a golden medal.
explanation.definitionFit: An epaulet is an ornamental shoulder piece on a uniform.

clue.text: Carriage taking medic round hospital in heaven

parts.note: Dr is short for doctor, a medic
O is round in shape

indicators.note: in means the hospital letter goes inside the heaven word

parts.note: the sky is the heavens

explanation.surface: A vehicle carries a doctor around a celestial hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: A droshky is a low four-wheeled Russian carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A droshky is a Russian horse-drawn carriage.

clue.text: Begin to apprehend outlaw, being reliable

indicators.note: to apprehend is to seize, so one word holds the other inside

parts.note: to begin is to start

indicators.note: out means the letters of law are put out of order

explanation.surface: The sheriff starts to arrest a fugitive and proves dependable.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'outlaw' must be split: 'out' is the anagram signal for 'law', and 'to apprehend' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalwart means loyal and dependable, a synonym for reliable.

clue.text: Holy person's abundant friction

parts.note: St is short for saint, a holy person
rife means plentiful, abundant

explanation.surface: A saint has plenty of conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: Strife is bitter conflict, friction between people.

clue.text: Many stay around to provide support for member

indicators.note: around means one word encloses the other

parts.note: to stay is to arrest or halt
M, the Roman thousand, means many

explanation.surface: Lots of people linger to give a hand to a club member.
explanation.definitionFit: An armrest supports the arm, a member of the body.

clue.text: Train for uterine disorder

indicators.note: disorder means the letters are put into disarray

explanation.surface: A course of treatment for a womb complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' is not exercise but a group of attendants.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is a train of attendants following an important person.

clue.text: Serve drinks, keeping a beast as lover

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside

parts.note: to serve drinks is to pour
a ram is a beast, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A barman keeps an animal while serving, as if it were a sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: A paramour is an illicit lover.

clue.text: Stomach-turning goddess of change

indicators.note: turning means the word for stomach is turned backwards

parts.note: tum is a childish word for stomach
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: A nauseating deity presides over transformation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stomach-turning' looks like 'revolting' but splits into TUM and its reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutate is to change form, as in a genetic alteration.

clue.text: Volunteers to tear up animal

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to rip is to tear

explanation.surface: Volunteers shred a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapir is a hoofed mammal with a short trunk.

clue.text: Lacking energy, hopeless — found God out here?

definitions.text: Lacking energy, hopeless — found God out here?

indicators.note: out means the gathered letters are thrown out of order
lacking means one letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A despairing pilgrim, drained and hopeless, wonders whether this was where faith was discovered.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop an E from HOPELESS ('Lacking energy') to get HOPLESS, then 'out' shuffles it with FOUND GOD. The Slough of Despond is the bog of despair in Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunyan's swamp of despair is where Christian sinks before reaching faith, a place of hopelessness.

clue.text: Old solvers (singular and plural) on big wheel

parts.note: an archaic singular 'you', addressing the solver
an archaic plural 'you'

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned forms of address are listed beside a fairground ride.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket tells you to give 'you' in old forms twice, the singular and then the plural. The London Eye is the giant Ferris wheel on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: The London Eye is the giant observation wheel beside the Thames.

clue.text: Want food to lead to victory

parts.note: to star is to take the lead role
VE is victory, as in VE Day, Victory in Europe

explanation.surface: Hunger drives someone on to triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: VE Day (8 May 1945) marked victory in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve is to go without food, to be in want of it.
